headline: Semis and Energy Lead a Fractured Tape as Rate Fears Grip the Broader Market
body_html:
Midway through Tuesday's session, the market is wearing a deeply split complexion. Declining issues outnumber advancers by nearly two to one — 350 names lower against 193 higher across the 545-stock universe — as investors grapple with the prospect of multiple Federal Reserve rate hikes over the next twelve months. A CNBC survey now projects at least two additional increases, and U.S. Treasury ten-year yields have pushed to their highest level since 2007, dragging bonds sharply lower and rattling rate-sensitive corners of equities.

Two sectors are bucking the pressure. Semiconductors lead the tape with a gain of roughly 1.4%, energized by outsized moves in RF-chip names Skyworks Solutions and Qorvo, up 10.1% and 7.1% respectively. Energy is close behind at plus 1.3%, with Middle East tensions — Houthi strikes on Saudi targets and dwindling Strait of Hormuz traffic — keeping crude elevated and lifting oil-linked names. The dollar's modest advance alongside firmer rate-hike odds is adding further tailwind to the energy complex.

Pressure is sharpest in Consumer, off more than 1%, and Software, down a comparable margin. Boot Barn leads decliners with a drop of 7.4%, joined by National Vision and American Eagle. Into the close, watch Treasury yields and any Hormuz-related headlines for the tape's direction.

briefs.headline: Forgent Power Solutions Surges to Session's Top Spot
briefs.body: Forgent Power Solutions is the standout mover midday, climbing 12.2% to lead the entire universe. The industrials-power name is drawing attention amid elevated energy-infrastructure interest, though no specific corporate catalyst has been publicly confirmed. Primoris Services, another construction-energy name, is also higher by 4.9%.

briefs.headline: Hormuz Disruption Keeps Oil Markets on Edge
briefs.body: Shipping traffic through the Strait of Hormuz is thinning as Middle East hostilities intensify, according to Reuters reporting. A fresh Houthi strike on Saudi targets has added to the anxiety, even as Saudi civil defence declared the danger passed in six cities including Yanbu. The uncertainty is supporting crude prices and lifting energy equities broadly.

briefs.headline: Fed Survey Points to Prolonged Rate-Hike Cycle
briefs.body: A CNBC poll of market professionals indicates the Federal Reserve is expected to raise rates at least twice more over the coming year, reinforcing a higher-for-longer interest-rate backdrop. Ten-year Treasury yields have consequently touched their loftiest level since 2007, pressuring bond prices and increasing the cost of capital across growth-oriented equities.

briefs.headline: AWS Cloud Outage in Gulf Region Rattles Tech Sentiment
briefs.body: Amazon Web Services has been unable to restore access to a data zone in Bahrain and one UAE region following damage attributed to the regional conflict, Reuters reported. The disruption highlights the real-world infrastructure risks posed by Middle East hostilities and is adding a cautionary note for software and cloud-exposed names already under selling pressure today.

briefs.headline: Consumer Names Slide as Retail Sentiment Softens
briefs.body: The consumer sector is among Tuesday's weakest, down roughly 1.1% in aggregate. Boot Barn is off 7.4%, National Vision has shed 5.3%, and American Eagle Outfitters is lower by 4.1%. The declines reflect a combination of rate-driven demand concerns and a broader pullback from discretionary spending names.

briefs.headline: LNG Outlook Brightens on Post-Conflict Demand Rebound Expectations
briefs.body: Analysts cited by Reuters project that liquefied natural gas demand across China, India and Pakistan is positioned to recover once the U.S.-Iran conflict concludes. The forward-looking view is lending additional support to energy names in today's session, complementing the near-term price lift already flowing from Hormuz supply-chain uncertainty.
